Explanation of the words:

Alif-Lam-Mim (الۤمۤ): This is one of the disjointed letters (al-huruf al-muqatta'a). It is written الۤمۤ and read alif, lam, meem.

Ghulibat (غُلبت): That is, Persia (Faris) overcame the Romans.

Al-Rum (الروم): A man's name. He is Rum ibn 'Aysu ibn Ishaq ibn Ibrahim, and the tribe was named after him because he was its ancestor.

Fi adna al-ard (في أدنى الأرض): That is, the nearest land of the Romans to Persia. It is a land called al-Jazirah, "between the Tigris and the Euphrates."

Wa hum min ba'di ghalabihim sayaghlibun (وهم من بعد غلبهم سيغلبون): That is, the Romans, after their defeat by Persia, will overcome Persia.

Fi bid' sinin (في بضع سنين): That is, within a period between three and nine years.

Lillahi al-amru min qablu wa min ba'du (لله الأمر من قبل ومن بعد): That is, the affair in this matter, both the Persian victory first and the Roman victory last, belongs to Allah alone, for whatever He wills comes to be, and whatever He does not will does not come to be.

Wa yawma'idhin yafrahu al-mu'minun (ويومئذ يفرح المؤمنون): That is, on the day the Romans overcome Persia, the believers rejoice at the victory of the People of the Book over the fire-worshipping polytheists, and at their own victory over the polytheists at Badr.

Wa'd Allah (وعد الله): That is, Allah promised them a promise and fulfilled it for them.

La yukhlifu Allah wa'dahu (لا يخلف الله وعده): That is, it is not in the nature of Allah to break a promise, because of the perfection of His power and knowledge.

Wa lakinna akthara al-nasi la ya'lamun (ولكن أكثر الناس لا يعلمون): The perfection of Allah's power and knowledge, which necessitates the fulfilment of His promise.

Ya'lamuna zahiran min al-hayat al-dunya (يعلمون ظاهراً من الحياة الدنيا): That is, they do not know the realities of faith or the secrets of the Law, but know only what appears of worldly life, such as seeking a livelihood through trade, agriculture and crafts.

Wa hum 'an al-akhirati hum ghafilun (وهم عن الآخرة هم غافلون): That is, heedless of the Hereafter and what is in it of bliss and blaze, and of what leads to that through beliefs, actions and abstentions.

Meaning of the verses:

Allah's words, ﴿Alif-Lam-Mim﴾: The best approaches to interpreting such letters is to say that Allah knows best what He intends by them, while noting that they serve two purposes. The second is that, since the polytheists used to prevent people from listening to the Qur'an for fear of its effect on the listener, He, exalted is He, brought such openings to many of the surahs of His Book, which compelled them to listen to it, because these letters were not familiar in their speech.

Allah's words, ﴿The Romans have been overcome﴾: That is, Persia overcame the Romans ﴿in the nearest land﴾, meaning the land of al-Sham nearest to the lands of Persia, namely the land of al-Jazirah lying between the rivers Tigris and Euphrates. His words, ﴿within a few years﴾: That is, within a period of time between three and nine years. His words, ﴿To Allah belongs the command, before and after﴾: That is, the command in this matter belongs to Allah, Exalted, both before the defeat and after it, since He is the one who disposes of His creation.

His words, ﴿And on that day the believers will rejoice in the victory of Allah﴾: That is, on the day the Romans overcome the Persians, the believers will rejoice at the Roman victory over the Persians, because the Romans are People of the Book while the Persians are polytheists who worship fire. Just as the believers also rejoice at their own victory over the polytheists at Badr, since the time when the Romans were victorious was the same time when the believers were victorious over the polytheists at Badr. This is among the unseen matters that the Qur'an reported before they occurred; it happened as it had reported, and thereby it confirmed that Islam, its Book and its Messenger are true. His words, exalted is He, ﴿He gives victory to whom He wills, and He is the Mighty, the Merciful﴾: That is, Allah, Exalted, gives victory to whomever of His servants He wills to support. He willed to support the believers and the Romans, so He granted them victory at one time, thereby fulfilling His promise which He had promised them some years before. He is the Mighty, meaning the one who prevails over His affair, able to fulfil His promise, the Merciful toward His friends and righteous servants. His words, ﴿But most people do not know. They know the outward of the worldly life﴾: Such as the arrangement of Allah, His power, His might, the benefits of His Law and the secrets of His religion. Rather, they know only the outward of the worldly life, such as arranging their livelihood through agriculture, crafts and trade. At the same time they are heedless of the Hereafter, heedless of what they must do and avoid in order to be happy there, by being saved from the Fire and dwelling in the Gardens in the neighbourhood of the Most Merciful, glorified and exalted is He.

Guidance from the verses:

1) Confirmation of the truth of Islam and that it is the true religion, by the truthfulness of what its Book reports of unseen matters.

2) Clarification that the People of the Book, Jews and Christians, are closer to the Muslims than the polytheists and the atheists, such as the communist Bolsheviks who do not believe in Allah and the Last Day.

3) Clarification that most people do not know what would make them happy in the Hereafter and perfect them: the correct beliefs and the wise, merciful laws without which a person is neither perfected nor made happy. They know only the outward of worldly life, such as arranging livelihood through agriculture, crafts and trade. As for the secret of the worldly life and why it exists, they know nothing of it, and they are utterly heedless of the Hereafter, so they do not seek what would make them happy there or what would make them wretched. We seek refuge with Allah, Exalted, from heedlessness of the abode of everlasting life, whether in bliss or wretchedness.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 8–10:

Explanation of the words:

In themselves (fi anfusihim): that is, how they were created when they were nothing, and then how they became men.

Except with truth (illa bil-haqq): that is, God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with the truth, which is justice.

And a specified term (wa ajalin musamma): this is the end of this life, so that the second life may be the life of just recompense.

Indeed disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord (bi-liqa'i rabbihim la-kafirun): that is, in the resurrection and standing before God, where He questions them, reckons with them and recompenses them.

And they tilled the earth (wa atharu al-ard): they turned it over for ploughing, planting, building and cultivation.

And they cultivated it (wa 'amarūha): that is, they cultivated the earth more than these polytheists have cultivated it.

And their messengers came to them with clear proofs (wa jat'hum rusuluhum bil-bayyinat): that is, with evidences, arguments and proofs, including miracles and other things.

But they were wronging themselves (wa lakin kanu anfusahum yazlimun): that is, by their denial, their polytheism and their sins, so they exposed themselves to destruction.

Then the end of those who did evil was the worst (thumma kana 'aqibata alladhina asa'u al-su'a): that is, by denial, polytheism, and sins; al-su'a is the worse state.

Because they denied the signs of God (an kadhdhabu bi-ayat Allah): that is, because they denied the Qur'anic signs of God and mocked them.

Explanation of the verses:

The noble context continues calling those who deny the Last Resurrection to belief in it through the rational proofs contained in the Qur'anic verses. His saying, exalted is He, ﴿Do they not reflect within themselves?﴾ means: do they deny resurrection without reflecting on themselves, how they were non-existent, then came into being as infants, then youths, then men, middle-aged and elderly, and then die? Is not the One Who is able to create them, raise them and then cause them to die, able to resurrect them, reckon with them and recompense them for their deeds in this worldly life? His saying, exalted is He, ﴿God did not create the heavens and the earth and what is between them except with truth and for a specified term﴾ means: He did not create them in vain, but created them so that He may be remembered and thanked. Then, when the appointed term set for them is complete, He will annihilate them, then raise His servants to reckon with them: whether they remembered and gave thanks, or neglected, forgot and disbelieved; then He will recompense them according to their faith and obedience, or their disbelief and disobedience.

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Indeed, many of the people are disbelievers in the meeting with their Lord﴾ informs that, despite the manifestness of the proofs and the strength of the arguments for the soundness of the belief in resurrection and recompense, many people disbelieve in resurrection and recompense. His saying, exalted is He, in verse [9]: ﴿Have they not travelled through the earth and observed how was the end of those before them?﴾ means: will those polytheists deny resurrection and recompense, and not travel through the earth, north and south, and observe how was the end of those before them, destruction and ruin? ﴿They were stronger than them in power and they tilled the earth﴾ through building, cultivation, farming and agriculture, ﴿and cultivated it﴾ more than these people cultivated it. ﴿And their messengers came to them with clear proofs﴾. And when He destroyed them, He was not unjust to them, but they were the ones who wronged themselves. Is this not evidence of God's wisdom, knowledge and power? How, then, can His raising of His servants on the Day of Resurrection to reckon with them and recompense them be denied?

His saying, exalted is He: ﴿Then the end of those who did evil﴾ means: the deeds, so that they did not set them right, when they denied God's messengers and His laws. His saying: ﴿the worst﴾ means: the end of those who committed the worst evil, that is, their loss and destruction. His saying ﴿because they denied the signs of God﴾ means: because they denied God's signs ﴿and they used to mock them﴾ and persisted in that and did not repent.

Guidance from the verses:

1) Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense by mentioning the rational proofs that establish it.

2) The disbelief of most people in resurrection despite the abundance and strength of the proofs.

3) The legitimacy of travelling through the earth for reflection, on condition that no sin is incurred in doing so, through abandoning an obligation or committing a prohibited act.

4) Explanation of God's just recompense, that the end of evil-doing is the worst.

5) The disbelief of mocking the Shari'ah and its rulings, and the Qur'an and its verses.

This is the meaning of His statement, Exalted: ﴿So who will guide one whom Allah has sent astray?﴾, that is, no one. 5) The cause of people's misguidance is their following of their desires without knowledge, and their turning away from guidance through indulgence in following desire.

2) The Lord, Exalted, is singular in the highest description in every majesty and perfection.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 30–32:

Explanation of the words:

﴿Fa-aqim wajhaka lil-din hanifa﴾: That is, direct your face, O our Messenger, toward the religion of Islam such that you look at nothing but it.

Hanifan (ḥanīf, one who turns away from all other religions toward the truth): That is, inclining away from all other religions toward it, and it has the meaning of turning toward it wholeheartedly.

Fitrat Allah (fiṭra, the innate disposition): That is, the workmanship of God upon which He created the human being, which is his capacity to believe in God, exalted is He.

La tabdila li-khalq Allah (there is no alteration to the creation of God): That is, do not work to change that capacity for faith and monotheism. The sentence is declarative in form but imperative in meaning.

Al-din al-qayyim (the upright religion): That is, the straight path, whoever takes hold of it will not go astray.

Munibina ilayhi (turning penitently back to Him): That is, returning to Him, exalted is He, by doing what He loves and abandoning what He dislikes.

Wa kanu shiya' (and they became sects): That is, groups and factions, each party rejoicing in what it holds of truth and falsehood.

The meaning of the verses:

When the Exalted established the doctrine of monotheism, resurrection, and recompense with proofs, and included within this the doctrine of prophethood and its affirmation for the Prophet ﷺ, He commanded His Messenger, and the believers who follow him, saying: ﴿So direct your face toward the religion, inclining to it [as a ḥanīf]﴾. That is, set your faces, O Messenger and believers, toward the true religion, the religion of Islam, which rests upon the principle of monotheism and righteous deeds, so do not turn your attention to any other misguided, false religion. His saying ﴿the fitrah of God upon which He created mankind﴾ means: direct your faces toward the true religion upon which God created mankind with that fitrah, which is the creation of man as one capable of faith and monotheism. His saying: ﴿There is no alteration to the creation of God﴾ means: do not alter or change that creation, but rather nurture and bring it out through upbringing, until the child grows up upon faith and monotheism. The sentence is declarative in form but imperative in meaning, like His saying: ﴿So will you not desist?﴾, which means "desist," and is more emphatic than "desist"; so "there is no alteration" is more emphatic than "do not alter." His saying: ﴿That is the upright religion﴾ means the adherence to what man was created upon, namely faith in God and His monotheism, and manifesting that in reality through faith in God and in what He commanded to be believed (the pillars of faith), and through worship of God, which is obedience to Him by doing what He commands and avoiding what He forbids, sincerely for Him alone, without any of His other creatures sharing in it. This is the upright religion that man must hold to. His saying: ﴿But most of mankind do not know﴾ informs that most people do not know or recognize the upright religion which He has established, as He explained in the verses; and it is as He, glorified and exalted, has informed. His saying ﴿turning penitently back to Him﴾ means: set your faces toward the upright religion while being those who return to Him, exalted is He, repenting to Him from every religion other than this religion, and from every obedience other than His obedience, by doing His commands and avoiding His prohibitions. His saying: ﴿And fear Him﴾ means: fear Him, exalted is He, for His punishment is severe; so do not abandon His religion for any other religion, nor obey any authority other than God and His Messenger. His saying: ﴿And establish the prayer﴾ means: be diligent in it at its times, and perform it as He legislated it in its number and manner, for it is the watering of faith and the nurturing of awe and love of God, exalted is He. His saying, exalted is He: ﴿And do not be of the polytheists, of those who divided their religion and became sects﴾ forbids the believers, the people of the upright religion which is Islam, from being among the polytheists in any form of polytheism, in belief, speech, or deed.

Thus every creed other than Islam has adherents who are polytheists and disbelievers, whether they are Magians, Jews, Christians, Buddhists, Hindus, or Bolshevik communists, for all of them have divided their religion, which they ought to hold to, namely the religion of the fitrah, which is Islam, and they became sects, meaning divisions and parties, each faction championing what it holds and partisan toward it. So each party among them, with what they have of religion, rejoices in it, supposing that it is the true religion, while it is certainly falsehood, because it is not the religion of the fitrah upon which God created mankind, which is Islam, founded on the monotheism of God and His worship in the manner He legislated for His servants to worship Him, so that they may be perfected thereby and be happy.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The obligation to turn to God in worship and to be sincere to Him therein.

2) Islam is the religion of God, by which He created man as one qualified for it, and no religion other than it is accepted from him.

3) The obligation to turn penitently to God and to return to Him in every state.

4) The obligation of fearing God, mighty and majestic, and of establishing the prayer.

5) Disavowal of polytheism and polytheists.

6) The prohibition of division in the Islamic religion and the obligation of unity in it in belief, worship, and judgment.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 33–37:

Explanation of the words:

"And when harm touches people": that is, when harm touches the polytheists, a hardship such as sickness, poverty or drought.

"Turning back to Him (munibin ilayhi)": that is, returning to Him in humble supplication and prayer, to Him alone, exalted is He, and not to anyone else.

"Mercy": by removing the harm, or by sending rain, granting prosperity and abundance of provision.

"Ascribe partners (yushrikun)": that is, ascribe partners to their Lord, worshipping others alongside Him by sacrificing to idols, making vows to them and other such acts.

"So that they may deny what We have given them": that is, so that their thankfulness becomes a denial of His blessings, God forbid.

"Or have We sent down to them an authority (sultan)": that is, a proof from a scripture or otherwise, speaking of their polytheism, confirming it for them and commanding them to it.

"Because of what their hands have sent forth": that is, because of their sins and their departure from God's laws (sunan) in the order of life.

"Then they despair (idha hum yaqnatun)": that is, they lose hope of relief once the hardship is lifted.

"He extends provision to whom He wills": that is, He widens it as a test for him.

"And restricts it": that is, He narrows provision for whom He wills, as a trial.

Meaning of the verses:

When God commanded His Messenger and the believers to establish the religion and forbade them to be among the polytheists, who divided their religion and became sects, He informed us that the polytheists, when harm touches them, namely sickness and hardship such as drought and high prices or the like, call upon their Lord, turning back to Him in supplication and humble entreaty, invoking none other. This is His saying, "And when harm touches people, they call upon their Lord, turning back to Him" (30:33). And His saying, "Then when He lets them taste mercy from Him" (30:33): He grants them mercy from Himself, which is health, ease, fertility and the like. "Behold, a group of them" (30:33), that is, a large number, "ascribe partners to their Lord" (30:33), worshipping idols and images in various kinds of worship. And His saying, "So that they may deny what We have given them" (30:34): they ascribed partners to God after His bounty upon them, so as to deny the blessing of relief from harm that He granted them. "Then enjoy yourselves, for you will soon know" (30:34), O disbelievers, the blessings God has bestowed upon you. You will come to know the outcome of your denial of God's blessings and your association of others with Him on the day you are returned to Him barefoot, naked, with no protector or helper besides Him, exalted is He.

And His saying: "Or have We sent down to them an authority, so that it speaks of what they used to associate with Him?" (30:35). That is: what has encouraged them to polytheism and made them persist in it, so that when they abandon it in the hour of hardship they return to it in the hour of ease? Have We sent down to them an authority, that is, a proof from a scripture or the like, which speaks of their polytheism, confirms it for them and commands them to it? By God, no! Rather, it is ignorance, blind imitation and obstinacy. And His saying: "And when We let people taste mercy, they rejoice in it" (30:36). This is the state of the people of polytheism, disbelief and ignorance: when God lets them taste mercy of abundance, ease and health, they rejoice in it with the joy of insolence and arrogance. "But if an evil befalls them" (30:36), such as dearth, drought, sickness or poverty, "because of what their hands have sent forth" (30:36), of sins and disobedience, among them the violation of God's laws in the cosmos, "then they despair" (30:36), that is, they lose hope of relief. This is because of their disbelief in God and their ignorance of His names and attributes.

And His saying: "Do they not see that God extends provision to whom He wills and restricts it?" (30:37). That is: have they not seen with their own eyes that God extends provision, widening it for whom He wills as a test, to see whether he gives thanks or disbelieves; and restricts it, narrowing provision for whom He wills as a trial, to see whether he endures patiently or grows restless and resentful? For if they had eyes with which to see and hearts with which to understand, they would not have despaired of God's mercy and relief, nor would they have lost hope. And His saying: "Indeed in that are signs" (30:37), that is, in the aforementioned governance of God over His creation through giving and withholding, "signs" that is, proofs and indications guiding the believers to God's power, kindness, mercy and wisdom in governing His dominion and kingdom. Glory be to Him, the Mighty God and the Lord, Most Forgiving, Most Merciful.

Guidance of the verses:

1) The ignorance of the polytheists and the corruption of their minds, as shown by the attributes and conditions God has mentioned concerning them.

2) God's warning to those who persist in polytheism and disbelief of the punishment of the Day of Resurrection.

3) The state of the people of polytheism, disbelief and ignorance: their joy at blessings is the joy of insolence and arrogance, and their despair and hopelessness when trial and hardship befall them.

4) The manifestation of God's wisdom and governance in provision, both in widening and in restricting it. Comprehending this is specific to the believers, because they are alive, they see and understand, unlike the disbelievers, who are dead, with no sight and no comprehension.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 38–40:

Explanation of the words:

﴿So give to the near of kin their right﴾: that is, give the relatives their due of kindness and maintaining ties.

"The needy" (al-miskin): that is, the destitute who has no wealth; give him his due in food, drink and clothing.

"The wayfarer" (ibn al-sabil): that is, give the traveller, i.e. the one on a journey, his due in shelter and food.

﴿That is better﴾: that is, that spending is better than not spending for those who seek the Face of God, the Exalted, for their Lord rewards them with the finest reward.

﴿And what you give in riba﴾: that is, a gift or present; it is called riba because they intend by it to increase their wealth.

﴿That it may increase within the wealth of people﴾: that is, so that by means of what you give them, which they return to you, the little you gave may be returned to you as much.

﴿It does not increase with God﴾: that is, God does not bless it and does not multiply its reward.

﴿Those are the ones who multiply﴾: that is, those who give their wealth as charity seeking the Face of God; these are the ones whose reward is multiplied manifold.

﴿Is there of your partners﴾: that is, of your idols that you worship?

﴿Who does any of that?﴾: the answer is none; so their divinity is nullified and worshipping them is forbidden.

﴿Glory be to Him and exalted is He above what they associate﴾: that is, the Lord is exalted above association and high above the polytheists.

The meaning of the verses:

When God, exalted is He, explained in the preceding verse that He extends provision to whom He wills as a trial and restricts it for whom He wills as a test, He commanded His Messenger and his community who follow him to give the near of kin their due, and the needy and the wayfarer, since withholding obligatory rights neither increases the breadth of provision nor narrows it, for the expansion and restriction of provision return to the wise and knowing disposition of God, the Exalted. This is what His words indicate: ﴿So give to the near of kin their right﴾, that is, of kindness and maintaining ties; ﴿and the needy﴾, who does not possess his sustenance; ﴿and the wayfarer﴾, the traveller who arrives in a town and knows no one there. Their right is shelter, feeding and clothing them. His words ﴿That is better for those who seek the Face of God﴾: that is, that giving of rights is better in state and outcome for those who seek the Face of God, the Exalted, and what He has of reward. His words: ﴿And those are the successful﴾: that is, those who win deliverance from punishment in this world and the Hereafter, and entry into Paradise on the Day of Resurrection. His words, exalted is He: ﴿And what you give in riba so that it may increase within the wealth of people, it does not increase with God﴾: that is, what you give of gifts and presents, desiring that more be returned to you than you gave, this giving does not increase with God, and its reward is not multiplied, nor is one rewarded for it. His words: ﴿And what you give in zakah﴾: that is, charities by which you seek the Face of God, that He may be pleased with you, forgive you and have mercy upon you. ﴿Those are the ones﴾: that is, those who spend seeking the Face of God, ﴿they are the ones who multiply﴾: that is, those for whom the reward and recompense are multiplied.

If so, why do you worship them besides God? Where do your minds go, O polytheists?

﴿That is better﴾: that is, that spending is better than not spending for those who seek the Face of God, the Exalted, for their Lord rewards them with the finest reward.

﴿And what you give in riba﴾: that is, a gift or present; it is called riba because they intend by it to increase their wealth.

﴿That it may increase within the wealth of people﴾: that is, so that by means of what you give them, which they return to you, the little you gave may be returned to you as much.

﴿Those are the ones who multiply﴾: that is, those who give their wealth as charity seeking the Face of God; these are the ones whose reward is multiplied manifold.

When God, exalted is He, explained in the preceding verse that He extends provision to whom He wills as a trial and restricts it for whom He wills as a test, He commanded His Messenger and his community who follow him to give the near of kin their due, and the needy and the wayfarer, since withholding obligatory rights neither increases the breadth of provision nor narrows it, for the expansion and restriction of provision return to the wise and knowing disposition of God, the Exalted. His words ﴿That is better for those who seek the Face of God﴾: that is, that giving of rights is better in state and outcome for those who seek the Face of God, the Exalted, and what He has of reward. Among the lessons of the verses:

1) The obligation to give relatives their rights of kindness and maintaining ties.

2) The obligation to provide for the poor and the wayfarers in the Islamic community.

3) The permissibility of a worldly-reward gift, such as a man giving something while wanting more in return but having no reward for it in the Hereafter; this gift is called "gift of reward" (hibat al-thawab), and it is forbidden for the Messenger, based on God's words to him: ﴿And do not give, seeking to receive more﴾ [al-Muddaththir: 6].

5) Refutation of polytheism, censure of the polytheists, and explanation of their ignorance and the misguidance of their minds.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 41–45:

Explanation of the words:

بما كسبت أيدي الناس (Bima kasabat aydi al-nas): i.e., because of what the hands of people earned of injustice and transgression.

ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا (Liyudhiqahum ba'da alladhi 'amilu): i.e., this came to pass and happened so that Allah would make them taste the punishment for some of their sins.

لعلهم يرجعون (La'allahum yarji'un): so that they would turn back from sins to obedience and steadfastness.

قل سيروا في الأرض (Qul siru fi al-ard): i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to the people of Makkah who deny you and associate partners with Allah: "Travel."

عاقبة الذين من قبل ('Aqibat alladhina min qabl): i.e., how was the end of those who denied their messengers and associated partners with their Lord? It was their destruction.

فأقم وجهك للدين القيم (Fa-aqim wajhaka lil-din al-qayyim): i.e., remain steadfast in obedience to your Lord, worshipping Him, conveying His message, and implementing His rulings.

لا مرد له من الله (La marudda lahu min Allah): i.e., Allah does not turn it back, because He has decreed its coming, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

يصدعون (Yasda'un): i.e., they separate into two groups.

يمهدون (Yumahhidun): i.e., they spread out and prepare for themselves resting places in the Garden through their faith and righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context previously established the refutation of polytheism by rational proof, yet the polytheists insist on their polytheism, and therefore corruption will inevitably appear on earth. Allah the Exalted informs us of this in His words in this noble verse [41]: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea﴾, i.e., sins have spread on land, at sea, and in the air today, so other than Allah is worshipped, His sacred prohibitions are violated, and people are harmed in their wealth, bodies, and honor. This is the result of turning away from the religion of Allah, neglecting its laws, and failing to implement its rulings. His words ﴿because of what the hands of people have earned﴾, i.e., because of their injustice, disbelief, wickedness, and debauchery. His words "so that He may make them taste some of what they have done": i.e., whatever drought, famine, high prices, wars, and tribulations befall them, Allah has only afflicted them with it ﴿so that He may make them taste some of what they have done﴾ of polytheism and sins, not all of what they did, for if He had seized them for all their sins, He would have ended their lives and eliminated their existence. But He is the Most Merciful to His servants, the Gentle with them. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see how was the end of those before﴾. Say, O Our Messenger, to the disbelieving Quraysh who deny you and associate partners with their Lord: travel through the earth, northward, southward, or westward, and look with your own eyes at how was the end of those who denied their messengers and disbelieved in their Lord before you. It was devastation and destruction. Would you then be pleased to be like them? His words ﴿Most of them were polytheists﴾: i.e., most of those destroyed peoples were polytheists, so the polytheism and denial in which you are engaged is the cause of their destruction and ruin. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾: i.e., remain steadfast, O Our Messenger, you and the believers with you, upon the religion of Islam, for no religion other than it is accepted. So believe in its creed, comply with its commands, avoid its prohibitions, adopt its manners, embody its morals, establish its limits, make lawful what it makes lawful, forbid what it forbids, call to it, and teach it to all people, and be patient in this, for the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing. His words: ﴿Before there comes a Day that cannot be turned back from Allah﴾: i.e., do what I have commanded you before the coming of the Day of Resurrection, when there will be no action but only recompense. His words ﴿that cannot be turned back from Allah﴾: i.e., Allah will not turn it back when its appointed time comes, because He has decreed its coming without doubt, for the recompense of deeds done in this world.

His words ﴿On that Day they will be separated﴾: i.e., on the day that comes, the day that cannot be turned back, they will split into two groups, just as a wall splits into two parts: a group in the Garden and a group in the Fire. His words: ﴿Whoever disbelieves, upon him is his disbelief﴾: i.e., whoever disbelieves today, the consequence of his disbelief will return upon him on the Day of Resurrection. ﴿And whoever does righteousness﴾: i.e., today, ﴿for themselves they prepare﴾: i.e., they spread out their bedding in the Garden, since the benefit of their righteous deeds returns to them and not to others. His words ﴿Indeed, He does not love the disbelievers﴾: this sentence is the reason for an omitted sentence, the implied meaning being: and He will recompense the disbelievers with His justice, which is the evil of punishment, because He does not love the disbelievers.

Guidance from the verses:

1) The appearance of corruption in the form of drought and high prices, or war and disease, is preceded, according to the custom of Allah, by the appearance of corruption in beliefs through polytheism, and in deeds through wickedness and sins.

2) The obligation of steadfastness upon the Islamic religion in creed, worship, judgment, and rule.

3) Affirmation of the belief in resurrection and recompense by mentioning its events and occurrences.

4) Clarification that Allah the Exalted loves the God-fearing and dislikes the disbelievers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 41–45:

Explanation of the words:

ظهر الفساد في البر والبحر (Zahara al-fasad fi al-barr wa al-bahr): i.e., sins appeared on land and sea, and evil and corruption followed them.

بما كسبت أيدي الناس (Bima kasabat aydi al-nas): i.e., because of what the hands of people earned of injustice and transgression.

ليذيقهم بعض الذي عملوا (Liyudhiqahum ba'da alladhi 'amilu): i.e., this came to pass and happened so that Allah would make them taste the punishment for some of their sins.

لعلهم يرجعون (La'allahum yarji'un): so that they would turn back from sins to obedience and steadfastness.

قل سيروا في الأرض (Qul siru fi al-ard): i.e., say, O Our Messenger, to the people of Makkah who deny you and associate partners with Allah: "Travel."

عاقبة الذين من قبل ('Aqibat alladhina min qabl): i.e., how was the end of those who denied their messengers and associated partners with their Lord? It was their destruction.

فأقم وجهك للدين القيم (Fa-aqim wajhaka lil-din al-qayyim): i.e., remain steadfast in obedience to your Lord, worshipping Him, conveying His message, and implementing His rulings.

لا مرد له من الله (La marudda lahu min Allah): i.e., Allah does not turn it back, because He has decreed its coming, and it is the Day of Resurrection.

يصدعون (Yasda'un): i.e., they separate into two groups.

يمهدون (Yumahhidun): i.e., they spread out and prepare for themselves resting places in the Garden through their faith and righteous deeds.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context previously established the refutation of polytheism by rational proof, yet the polytheists insist on their polytheism, and therefore corruption will inevitably appear on earth. Allah the Exalted informs us of this in His words in this noble verse [41]: ﴿Corruption has appeared on land and sea﴾, i.e., sins have spread on land, at sea, and in the air today, so other than Allah is worshipped, His sacred prohibitions are violated, and people are harmed in their wealth, bodies, and honor. This is the result of turning away from the religion of Allah, neglecting its laws, and failing to implement its rulings. His words ﴿because of what the hands of people have earned﴾, i.e., because of their injustice, disbelief, wickedness, and debauchery. His words "so that He may make them taste some of what they have done": i.e., whatever drought, famine, high prices, wars, and tribulations befall them, Allah has only afflicted them with it ﴿so that He may make them taste some of what they have done﴾ of polytheism and sins, not all of what they did, for if He had seized them for all their sins, He would have ended their lives and eliminated their existence. But He is the Most Merciful to His servants, the Gentle with them. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿Say: Travel through the earth and see how was the end of those before﴾. Say, O Our Messenger, to the disbelieving Quraysh who deny you and associate partners with their Lord: travel through the earth, northward, southward, or westward, and look with your own eyes at how was the end of those who denied their messengers and disbelieved in their Lord before you. His words ﴿Most of them were polytheists﴾: i.e., most of those destroyed peoples were polytheists, so the polytheism and denial in which you are engaged is the cause of their destruction and ruin. His words, may He be exalted: ﴿So set your face toward the upright religion﴾: i.e., remain steadfast, O Our Messenger, you and the believers with you, upon the religion of Islam, for no religion other than it is accepted. So believe in its creed, comply with its commands, avoid its prohibitions, adopt its manners, embody its morals, establish its limits, make lawful what it makes lawful, forbid what it forbids, call to it, and teach it to all people, and be patient in this, for the final outcome belongs to the God-fearing. His words: ﴿Before there comes a Day that cannot be turned back from Allah﴾: i.e., do what I have commanded you before the coming of the Day of Resurrection, when there will be no action but only recompense. His words ﴿that cannot be turned back from Allah﴾: i.e., Allah will not turn it back when its appointed time comes, because He has decreed its coming without doubt, for the recompense of deeds done in this world.

His words ﴿On that Day they will be separated﴾: i.e., on the day that comes, the day that cannot be turned back, they will split into two groups, just as a wall splits into two parts: a group in the Garden and a group in the Fire. **Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on Surah 30, verses 46–47:**

**Explanation of the words:**

**﴿وَمِنْ آيَاتِهِ أَنْ يُرْسِلَ الرِّيَاحَ﴾:** That is, among His proofs that point to His power to resurrect and to requite, and that make worship of Him alone obligatory.

**﴿مُبَشِّرَاتٍ﴾:** That is, bringing good news to the servants of the rain and its nearness.

**﴿وَلِيُذِيقَكُم مِّن رَّحْمَتِهِ﴾:** That is, through the rain, fertility, ease, and abundance of provision.

**﴿وَلِتَبْتَغُوا مِن فَضْلِهِ﴾:** That is, that you may seek provision from His vast bounty through trade by sea.

**﴿وَلَعَلَّكُمْ تَشْكُرُونَ﴾:** That is, so that you may give thanks for these blessings, and thereby believe and affirm the oneness of your Lord.

**﴿رُسُلًا إِلَىٰ قَوْمِهِمْ﴾:** That is, such as Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them.

**﴿فَجَاءُوهُم بِالْبَيِّنَاتِ﴾:** That is, with proofs and miracles.

**﴿الَّذِينَ أَجْرَمُوا﴾:** That is, those who corrupted their souls and made them foul with the traces of polytheism and sins.

**﴿حَقًّا عَلَيْنَا نَصْرُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ﴾:** That is, and We have made the victory of the believers a truth, and have made it binding upon Ourselves, so it will certainly come to pass.

**The meaning of the verses:**

The noble context continues to establish the divinity of God Most High, His justice and His mercy. He says: ﴿And among His signs﴾, that is, among Our signs that point to Our divinity, Our justice in Our creation, and Our mercy toward Our servants, is that We send the winds bearing good news of the nearness of rain, by which the lands and the people have life. Sending the winds is a matter that none can accomplish but God, and a management that falls short of every other management, and a mercy that surpasses every mercy. His saying ﴿and that He may let you taste of His mercy﴾, that is, by sending down rain, which results in fertility and ease. His saying ﴿and that the ships may run﴾, that is, the ships on the sea, since before the discovery of steam, the winds were what propelled ships on the sea, small and large. His saying ﴿by His command﴾, that is, by His permission, will and wise management. His saying ﴿and that you may seek of His bounty﴾, that is, that you may seek provision through trade by sea, from one region to another, carrying goods to sell and buy. His saying ﴿and perhaps you will be thankful﴾, that is, God Most High did this for you, subjecting it to you and enabling you to do it, in hope that you would thank your Lord by believing in Him, obeying Him, and affirming His oneness in worship. So, O servants of God, will you be thankful? His saying ﴿And We had certainly sent before you﴾, O Our Messenger, ﴿messengers to their peoples﴾, such as Nuh, Hud, Salih, Ibrahim, Lut and Shu'ayb, peace be upon them, and they came to their peoples with clear proofs and luminous arguments, just as you came with your people. Those peoples denied their messengers, ﴿so We took vengeance upon those who committed crimes﴾, and destroyed them, and We saved those who believed. ﴿And it was truly incumbent upon Us to aid the believers.﴾ Let Quraysh take heed from this; otherwise the vengeance of God will befall them, and God will destroy the criminals and save His Messenger and the believers, as is His way with the former peoples. And praise be to God, Lord of the worlds.

**Guidance from the verses:**

1. Affirming the lordship of God, which necessitates His divinity, by mentioning the manifestations of His power, knowledge, mercy and justice.

2. Explaining that God bestows blessings upon His servants so that they may thank Him by worshipping Him and affirming His oneness in worship. If they deny those blessings and do not thank God for them, He punishes them as He wills, how and when He wills.

3. Explaining that God takes vengeance on the criminals however long the time, and likewise aids the believers.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 48–53:

Explanation of the words:

"فتثير سحاباً" (fa-tuthīru saḥāban): that is, it stirs and agitates it, so that it moves and spreads.

"ويجعله كسفا" (wa-yajʿaluhu kisafan): that is, scattered pieces in the sky, here and there.

"فترى الودق" (fa-tara al-wadq): that is, the rain comes out from among the clouds.

"إذا هم يستبشرون" (idhā hum yastabshirūn): that is, rejoicing at the falling rain, for their watering.

"لمبلسين" (lamublisīn): that is, despairing and hopeless of its being sent down upon them.

"إن ذلك لمحيي الموتى" (inna dhālika la-muḥyī al-mawtā): that is, He who is able to send down rain and revive the earth after its death is able to revive the dead, and He is God, exalted.

"فرأوه مصفرا" (fa-ra'awhu muṣfarran): that is, they saw the plants and crops yellowed by the calamity that struck them, which was the scorching east wind (al-dabūr).

"لظلوا من بعده يكفرون" (la-ẓallū min baʿdihi yakfurūn): that is, they remained, after the destruction of their crops and plants, ungrateful for the blessings of God upon them previously.

"إن تسمع إلا من يؤمن بآياتنا" (in tasmaʿu illā man yu'minu bi-āyātinā): that is, you do not hear except from those who believe in God's signs.

Meaning of the verses:

The noble context continues in establishing the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mentioning manifestations of God's power in the cosmos. God, exalted, says: ﴿God is He who sends the winds﴾, that is, He creates them and dispatches them from their places of existence, "so they stir up clouds", that is, they disturb and move them, and He, exalted, spreads them in the sky as He wills, in density, lightness, abundance and scarcity, "and makes them into fragments", that is, pieces, "and you see the rain coming out from within it", that is, from between the parts of the cloud. His saying "then when He smites with it" means with the rain, "whomever He wills of His servants, behold, they rejoice", that is, those struck by the rain in their lands "rejoice", that is, are glad. "And though they were, before it was sent down upon them" — that is, the rain — "before it, certainly despairing", that is, distressed, grieved and hopeless. His saying, exalted: ﴿So look at the traces of God's mercy﴾, that is, look, O our Messenger, at the traces of God's mercy, that is, at the traces of the rain: how you see the earth has turned green after dryness and come alive after death. When you see that, you know that the One who revived the earth after its death is able to revive the dead from their graves, and that will be on the Day of Resurrection. His saying ﴿and He is over all things Powerful﴾ is a justification of the greatness of His power, and that He is able to revive the dead and to do everything He wills. His saying ﴿And if We send a wind﴾, that is, by Our might and majesty, if We send a wind in which there is a whirlwind containing fire, which burns those plants and dries them, then those who yesterday were rejoicing, with the joy of insolence at the rain, will see them, "they become ungrateful", that is, with respect to their Lord; they say: this is nothing but expressions of anger and discontent, due to their ignorance and disbelief. His saying, exalted: ﴿So you cannot make the dead hear, nor can you make the deaf hear the call when they turn away, retreating﴾, that is, you, O our Messenger, cannot guide these disbelievers, because they are deaf who do not hear and blind who do not see, due to the sins that have covered their hearts, which has disabled their senses. You, by virtue of your humanity and limited power, cannot make the dead hear your speech so that they understand it and act upon it, just as you cannot make the deaf hear your call when they turn away retreating; for if they were facing you, you might make them understand even by gesture, but if they turn their backs on you, it is impossible to make them hear.

So, console yourself and do not grieve over them. His saying: ﴿You make none hear except those who believe in Our signs, and they are submitting﴾, that is, you do not make hear, with acceptance, submission and comprehension, except those who believe in Our signs, that is, except the believers who believed in God's signs, recognized His proofs, believed in Him and declared His oneness, "and they are submitting", that is, yielding, humble and obedient. These are the ones you can make hear and guide, by God's permission, to what perfects and makes them happy in both abodes.

Guidance from the verses:

1) Establishing the doctrine of resurrection and recompense by mentioning rational proofs and arguments.

2) Explaining how clouds are formed and rain descends, which is a manifestation of divine power and knowledge.

3) Describing the state of the disbeliever in times of ease and times of hardship: in hardship he despairs, and in ease he disbelieves, due to the corruption of his heart through ignorance of God and His signs.

4) Inferring the unseen from the present, perceptible evidence.

5) Explaining that disbelievers are dead, which is why they neither hear nor see, and that believers are alive because they hear and see, since life has its effects on a living body, and so does death.

Commentary of al-Jaza'iri (Aysar al-Tafasir) on surah 30, verses 58–60:

Explanation of the words:

﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾: that is, We have made for the people, in this Qur'an, every kind of example.

﴿every kind of example﴾: that is, every remarkable quality that catches the attention and stirs the conscience, like parables, so that perhaps they will be mindful, and so believe and affirm God's oneness.

﴿And if you were to bring them a sign﴾: that is, even if you were to bring these polytheists every extraordinary proof.

﴿You are but falsifiers﴾: that is, you, O Messenger, and the believers are nothing but falsifiers in what you say and call to, of belief in God's signs and of meeting Him.

﴿those who do not know﴾: that is, [who do not know] what God sent down to His Messenger and revealed to him of clear signs.

﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true﴾: that is, be patient, O Our Messenger, with their harm, for the final outcome is yours, since your Lord has promised it to you, and the promise of God is true.

﴿And let not those who are not certain make you impatient﴾: that is, let not these polytheists, who deny the meeting with God, move you to lightness and recklessness so that you abandon your call to your Lord.

Meaning of the verses:

After presenting many proofs, marshalling much evidence, and displaying scenes of the Resurrection in the preceding verses, affirming the doctrine of resurrection and recompense which the polytheists of Quraysh denied, God says: ﴿And We have certainly presented for the people in this Qur'an every kind of example﴾. That is, We have made for the people in this Qur'an every mode of speech and variety of comparison, and the presentation of events in striking images that awaken the senses and alert the conscience, all so that perhaps they will be mindful, believe, and be guided to the truth, and thus be saved and made happy. But most of them did not benefit from this. ﴿And if you were to bring them a sign﴾: that is, a proof, whether a miracle or otherwise, indicating your truthfulness and the soundness of your call and of what you brought, ﴿they would surely say, those who disbelieve﴾: that is, among them. ﴿You are but falsifiers﴾: that is, you, O Messenger, and the believers are nothing but people of falsehood in what you say and call to, of the true religion and the Last Resurrection. And His saying ﴿Thus does God seal the hearts of those who do not know﴾: that is, likewise is the sealing upon the hearts of the disbelievers, who, even if you brought them every sign, would not believe in it; for what has veiled their hearts and what has been sealed upon them has taken hold. God seals the hearts of those who do not know, since the darkness of ignorance, like the darkness of polytheism and disbelief, veils the hearts from understanding and perception, so no faith arises and no response to the call of truth occurs. And His saying ﴿So be patient; indeed, the promise of God is true﴾: God commands His Messenger to hold fast to patience in his call and to steadfastness upon it in the face of this stubborn disbelief, until God gives him victory, for He promised him victory in more than one verse, and the promise of God is true; it is imminent and does not fail. And His saying: ﴿And let not those who are not certain make you impatient﴾: that is, be patient, and let not the obstinacy and insistence of the polytheists upon disbelief and denial move you to lightness, recklessness, and folly by abandoning forbearance and patience. What is meant by "those who are not certain" is everyone who does not believe in God and His meeting with certainty, for this kind of people is the one who provokes a person and drives him to step outside decorum and courtesy, God forbid.

Lessons from the verses:

1) God's establishing of proof against people through the arguments of faith and the evidence of guidance which He has set forth in His Book.

2) The worst state of a person is when his heart is sealed because of the abundance of his sins, so that he no longer understands or comprehends anything. In the report: "Your love of a thing makes you blind and deaf."

3) The obligation of patience and of maintaining forbearance and deliberation, however much the ignorant act ignorantly.
